### G · Misses, regime columns, population

**L-S.23 THE MISS COLUMN** — "MISS COLUMN first-class: every unfilled order counted and its would-have outcome
printed at both targets." (contract :95-96)
READING:
- **A miss** is an order of the book of record inside the scored window (`known_at_ms ≤ W`) whose WALK-W status
  is `expired` or `cancelled` (L-S.16). Each carries `miss_class`: `touched_not_through` (`fill_i_touch` non-null)
  or `never_touched`. `unresolved_at_end` orders are listed apart and are not misses. Unfilled orders triggered in
  the strip are counted in the strip print and get no would-have (nothing past `W` is summarised, L-S.25).
- **The would-have walk** answers "what did the limit cost us": the same order taken AT THE TRIGGER CLOSE AS A
  TAKER. Entry price `c5[t]` on bar `t`; the frozen stop `S` and the frozen target levels; `R_wh = |c5[t] − S|`;
  walked from bar `t+1` by L-S.18 with the record's target test, bounded at `hi_W`; the time stop at `close5[t +
  T5]`; invalidation by L-S.19; booked ALL-TAKER — gross and fee by `BK.account_l` (entry leg at bar `t`), funding
  uncapped as on every range row (OD-10): `wh_net_r = acc["gross_r"] − acc["fee_r"] − acc["funding_r_uncapped"]`,
  in R of `R_wh`.
- **"At both targets"** = three variants per miss, each on the whole unit unless stated: `T1` (the only target is
  T1), `T2` (the only target is T2), and `split` (the book's own law: `Q` at T1, the rest at T2). Each files
  `wh_exit_reason`, `wh_reached` (the walk ended at its target), `wh_exit_close_ms`, `wh_net_r`, `wh_gross_r`.
- **A would-have target must be ahead of the would-have entry** — the geometry law's own principle (L-S.11). The
  entry here is `c5[t]`, not `L`, and the POC can lie at or behind it. If `d·(px(n_T1) − c5[t]) ≤ 0` (decided
  exactly, by the grid's comparisons), or the order's T1 is void, the `T1` variant does not exist (filed null
  with the reason `wh_t1_not_ahead` or `t1_void`) and `split` is the `T2` walk; if `d·(px(n_T2) − c5[t]) ≤ 0` the
  `T2` and `split` variants do not exist (`wh_t2_not_ahead`). Both classes are counted.
- **Why the trigger close and a taker fill.** It is the only counterfactual executable at decision time. Entry
  "at the limit" assumes a fill at a price the market never gave (and for `never_touched` a price never traded).
  Entry at the expiry close starts after the move the order missed and makes missing look cheap. Of the
  executable readings this is the one that cannot flatter the book: it shows the full run-away at the dearest toll.
- `S_miss` (key `[book, symbol, known_at_ms, variant]`, `variant` ∈ {`T1`, `T2`, `split`}, `book == "scored"`;
  pointed, not inlined) and the grid `S_MISS_GRID` (whole, keyed by `cell`): trigger era × direction ×
  `miss_class` × `variant` → `n, n_reached, mean wh_net_r, sum wh_net_r`. Tier-E, "no interval", no verdict word,
  NEVER netted into any book.
- Printed on the fill-sensitivity grid: `n_orders`, `n_filled` per rule, `n_missed` (L-S.16).
SOURCE: contract :95-96; X's refusal rows for misses (`reason` "miss" / "miss_nochild" / "fill_unresolved_at_pin",
`tc11x_sfp.py:672-685`) — no outcome there; OD-8, OD-10; scout U6 C15, R-22.
RIVALS: as argued. A would-have at maker rates — an unfilled maker order paid no maker fee; the chase is a taker.
A would-have whose target lies behind its own entry, walked anyway — a resting limit that is marketable when
placed, booked as a loss "at target": not an order.
FAILS-IF: F-SCALP (b) MISS-3 and (l) MISS-TABLE: the status partition `n_orders == filled + expired + cancelled +
unresolved` fails; a miss has a TICK fill in its window; a would-have row differs from the fixture's own walk; a
variant exists whose target is not ahead of `c5[t]`. Planted mutations: the would-have entered at the limit; a
filled order listed as a miss; the split walk booked at maker rates.

**L-S.24 REGIME COLUMNS** — "REGIME COLUMNS: 1h ATR tercile (trailing) · VA age · breadth · 4h tide age." (contract
:102-103)
READING: four stamps on every order row and every trade row of every arm, each as of the trigger close τ, Tier-E,
COLUMNS ONLY — no book is cut, gated or re-walked by them, and the only table is an occupancy grid of counts.
- **`atr1h_tercile`** — the trailing midrank of `ATR_1h[k1]` among that asset's last `vol_window` finite
  `ATR_1h` values ending at bar `k1` INCLUSIVE (X's LX-X1.7 / LX-X4.2 law, mirrored from
  `tc11x_pct.trailing_counts`): with `(lt, eq, n)` the counts below, equal and total, decided in integers —
  `T1` iff `3·(2·lt + eq) < 2·n`; `T2` iff `< 4·n`; else `T3`; `unbanded` when fewer than `vol_floor` values exist.
  The raw ATR, the asset's own series. `atr1h_lt`, `atr1h_eq`, `atr1h_n` are filed.
- **`va_age_1h`** — the filed `va_age` of row `k1` (bars since the 1h value regime began, L-V.16); never null on
  an order (PERM requires INSIDE, so a regime is alive).
- **`breadth_5`** and **`tide_age_4h`** (with `tide_band_4h`) — L-G's breadth of record and the asset's own 4h
  tide age of record, read AS FILED from the two tables L-G files at `TC12-C.tide` (L-G.10):
  `tide/breadth_4h.parquet` (key `[open_ms]`; the home-five determined-young count of L-G.11) and
  `tide/tide_bars_4h.parquet` (key `[asset, open_ms]`; the asset's own run and band), each at the last 4h bar with
  `close_ms ≤ τ` (`asof_index`). Their definitions are L-G's; this section adds none and re-derives no band. A
  bar that is not warm, or whose edges are undefined, files the column null with L-G's own flag beside it.
- `S_REGIME` (a grid, whole, keyed by `cell`): for the three LEVELLED columns (`atr1h_tercile`; `breadth_5`; the
  tide band) column × level × book → `n_orders, n_filled`; for the two AGES (`va_age_1h`, `tide_age_4h`), which
  have no levels and are given none here, per book `n`, minimum, lower hinge, median, upper hinge, maximum
  (L-V.18's hinge law, so no quantile level is typed). Counts and positions only; no outcome column.

X's `exit/build_manifest.json` `constants.vol_window`, `.vol_floor`; LX-X1.7, LX-X4.2, LX-X4.7; TC11
`LEANS.md:464-467` (L-S.2's "trailing 2,000-bar quantiles over a window ending at the entry bar inclusive");
L-V.16; L-G.10, L-G.11; L-0.10 (`TC12-C.tide`); scout U5 §2.15.
RIVALS: an expanding pooled prefix (the tide band's "trailing") — the filed precedent for an ATR tercile in the
scalper is the rolling window. NATR — X's twin. Outcome tables by regime level — a cut of the book the contract

**L-S.25 POPULATION, ERA, THE SCORED WINDOW, THE STRIP** — "(vs zero; HOLDOUT era ["era"]; five home assets; both
directions; …)" (contract :83-84); rulings O-9, O-23; disposition OD-14
READING:
- **Panel:** the five home assets (`E.CLASSIC5`, L-D's home panel object), pooled; both directions in one book.
- **A trade's instant is its FILL bar's close** (O-9: "holdout = entry-bar close after `1719791999000`"; L-X.24:
  `entry_close_ms` is "the 5m bar of the fill"): `entry_ms = open5[f]`, `entry_close_ms = close5[f]`, `era =
  E.era_of(entry_close_ms)` — `tuning` iff `entry_close_ms ≤ ERA_CUT`, else `holdout`. **The book of record is the
  rows of the TICK walk with `ERA_CUT < entry_close_ms ≤ W`.**
- **The scored window (O-9).** Every book is ridden with `hi = hi_W`, the last 5m bar closing `≤ W` (WALK-W); a
  position still open there is marked at that bar's close with `exit_reason = "corridor_end"`, so `exit_close_ms ≤
  W` on every row of every scored, ladder and Tier-E arm.
- **An ORDER's era is its trigger close** (`era_trigger = E.era_of(known_at_ms)`): an unfilled order has no entry
  bar. An order triggered at or before the cut and filled after it is a holdout TRADE and a tuning ORDER; at most
  one per asset and book can exist (one resting order), and the count is printed (`era_straddle`).
- **One walk, not one per era.** The scored book is the holdout slice of the full-corridor TICK walk (L-S.1); the
  same walk's every row with `entry_close_ms ≤ W` is the arm `tierE__full_corridor`. The walk is not restarted at
  the cut.
- **The strip (O-9, OD-14) — for every ridden arm.** WALK-PIN is run once per fill rule and once per ridden Tier-E
  arm; `strip.parquet` holds every arm's rows with `W < entry_close_ms ≤ PIN` under the column `arm`; the `strip`
  leaf prints `n` per arm and one pointer, no statistic. The ridden arms are `scored`, `ladder__touch`,
  `ladder__deep`, `tierE__panel17`, `tierE__rr_unfiltered` and `tierE__live_edge`; `tierE__full_corridor` is the
  same walk as `scored` and is not repeated — it appears in the strip sidecar's `n_by_arm` with `same_rows_as =
  "scored"`. Ridden, printed beside, never scored, never pooled: a count and a pointer are the only aggregates
  over strip rows anywhere.
- Trades of the TICK walk open at `W` are continued in `stage_s/open_at_w_continued.parquet` (their WALK-PIN exit
  beside their scored mark). The other walks' open-at-`W` trades are held by the prefix identity below and are
  continued in no table.
- **Prefix identity of the two rides, for every walk:** every WALK-PIN order and trade resolved at or before `W`
  equals its WALK-W row on every column; a trade OPEN at `W` is compared on its entry, stop, R, T1 and T2 levels,
  and on its T1 fill iff that fill happened at or before `hi_W` — else the WALK-W row's T1 must be unfilled; the
  WALK-W rows of the TICK walk marked `corridor_end` are exactly the keys of `open_at_w_continued`.
- **Stamps.** A scored-window table is stamped with the score edge; the strip, the order ledgers and every table
  that reads past `W` with the pin (L-0.13).
- **What is in-sample on these bars** is the label's business (L-S.29): the lookback and the traverse are
  tuning-fit and are out-of-sample on the holdout; the bars themselves are `pre_seen` (O-23, O-30).

entry (or event-anchor) bar's CLOSE … P-SCALP-2 names the holdout era, so it is scored there").

**L-S.28 THE PRE-NAMED KILL, EXHAUSTIVELY** — "PRE-NAMED KILL: NOT SUPPORTED if the through-tick book fails the
bar; CLOSED FOR GOOD if it fails under DEEP too; CLOSED if it clears only under TOUCH (the fill-sensitivity row is
part of the verdict text); one-asset dependence read by LOAO 3/5 and the single-trade share." (contract :104-106);
dispositions OD-13, OD-19
READING: the rule of record is L-X.9's, carried without change. For each fill book X ∈ {TOUCH, TICK, DEEP}, at the
seed of record and the SCALPER bar, exactly one of three states holds: `U(X)` = X is not PANEL COMPLETE (L-X.7's
clause (c) fails; its ruler is undefined; an EMPTY BOOK is the limiting case); `C(X)` = PANEL COMPLETE and clauses
(a) ∧ (b) of L-X.8 hold; `F(X)` = PANEL COMPLETE and (a) or (b) fails. `D` = fewer than `above_half_bar(N)`
leave-one-asset-out panels of the TICK book exclude zero from above (L-X.11; "3/5" parsed from :106). **A closure
word needs a MEASURED failure: a book whose ruler is undefined is not a failed book.** The ten cases partition
every outcome:

| TICK | D | DEEP | TOUCH | `verdict_of_record` | qualifier | the contract's clause |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| C | false | C | any | `SUPPORTED` | — | the positive case |
| C | false | F | any | `SUPPORTED` | `FILL-SENSITIVE (does not clear under DEEP)` | none |
| C | false | U | any | `SUPPORTED` | `FILL-SENSITIVE (DEEP PANEL INCOMPLETE)` | none |
| C | true | any | any | `NOT SUPPORTED` | `LOAO BELOW THE LINE (k/N above; passing when dropped: <assets>; failing when dropped: <assets>)` | "one-asset dependence read by LOAO 3/5" |
| U | any | any | any | `NOT SUPPORTED` | `PANEL INCOMPLETE (…)` / `EMPTY BOOK` and `TICK PANEL INCOMPLETE — closure not ruled` | none (the ruler is undefined) |
| F | any | C | any | `NOT SUPPORTED` | — | "fails the bar" |
| F | any | U | any | `NOT SUPPORTED` | `DEEP PANEL INCOMPLETE — closure not ruled` | "fails the bar"; DEEP not measured |
| F | any | F | C | `NOT SUPPORTED — CLOSED` | `(clears only under TOUCH)` | "clears only under TOUCH" ("fails under DEEP too" also holds: OPEN TO OPERATOR 6) |
| F | any | F | U | `NOT SUPPORTED — CLOSED` | `TOUCH PANEL INCOMPLETE — "for good" not ruled` | "fails under DEEP too"; TOUCH not measured |
| F | any | F | F | `NOT SUPPORTED — CLOSED FOR GOOD` | — | "fails under DEEP too", at every fill model |

- **One test.** m stays as parsed (:82); only the TICK book can produce `SUPPORTED` and only it spends the
  family's test. TOUCH and DEEP are ruled with the same ruler, seed, draws and bar and can only qualify a
  `SUPPORTED` cell or choose among the failure words. The fill-sensitivity row opens with the fixed sentence:
  "TOUCH and DEEP are fill-model twins, not tests: they are ruled at the family bar without a test of their own
  and can only qualify a SUPPORTED cell or choose among the failure words; an interval that excludes zero on
  either is not a result."
- **The unnamed cells.** TICK clears and DEEP fails or is not measured: the row stands, and says in its own cell
  that it does not survive, or was not measured under, a deeper fill. TICK fails and DEEP clears: the row fails
  and nothing is closed — a deeper book that clears is not evidence the idea is dead. TOUCH failing while TICK
  clears is possible because the books are sequenced separately (L-S.16); the word is TICK's and the
  fill-sensitivity row shows the inversion. Any `PANEL INCOMPLETE` book closes nothing beyond what the table says.
- **One-asset dependence** (the clause sits inside the kill; L-X.9 takes the reading that cannot flatter, and
  O-32 lets it stand): where the TICK book clears but LOAO does not reach 3/5, the word is `NOT SUPPORTED` with
  the qualifier `LOAO BELOW THE LINE (…)`, and the verdict text adds the fixed sentence "the contract reads
  one-asset dependence by this line (:106); a panel that fails when an asset is DROPPED leans on that asset, a
  panel that fails while an asset is KEPT is dragged by it". The single-trade share (L-X.12) has no threshold in
  the contract or on file; it is printed and decides nothing.
- **The verdict text** = the cell (word, qualifiers, label per L-S.29) + the fill-sensitivity row (the fixed
  sentence; then per fill rule the book's own `n`, point, interval, `p_num/p_den` and its state C / F / U; then
  the two booleans `fails_under_deep_too = F(TICK) ∧ F(DEEP)` and `clears_only_under_touch = F(TICK) ∧ F(DEEP) ∧
  C(TOUCH)`, which `SCORES.json rows[].fill_ladder` also carries) + the LOAO line `k/N` with its fixed sentence +
  the single-trade share of record + the per-order ladder counts of the TICK ledger and, where the three books'
  own n are not ordered, the line `BOOK-N-NOT-MONOTONE` (L-S.16; L-X.24) + beside the licence word the leaf
  `licence_at_maker_pin` (L-S.27) + beside the cost twins the sentence of L-S.22 on adverse selection.
- **What a closure forbids afterwards** — the standing lines the ledger append carries (L-X.32):
  - `NOT SUPPORTED` (with or without a `PANEL INCOMPLETE` qualifier): nothing is closed. The 1h maker licence
    stands; a later tier may register another 1h value-area range trade, `pre_seen` on these bars.
  - `NOT SUPPORTED — CLOSED`: this trade form — a resting limit at the 1h value edge on the 5m clock — is closed
    under every fill model that requires a trade-through. It is not re-registered on backtest fills; the only
    reopening path is evidence about the fill itself (queue position or live fills), ruled in by the operator.
  - `NOT SUPPORTED — CLOSED FOR GOOD`: scalper mode on the 1h value area at the maker toll is closed in this and
    every later tier; no fill model reopens it (it has a MEASURED failure at every fill model), and the "maker"
    ruling's one use is spent. Only a new operator ruling naming a new mechanism reopens the 1h lens for range
    trading.
  - A `CLOSED BY PRECONDITION` row closes nothing beyond what its failed record already says.

- **mechanism:** Inside a 1h value area that the 1h machine reports INSIDE, price that reaches the outer third
  near an edge tends to rotate back toward the POC and the far edge — the "edges respected" leg TC11-X licensed for
  the 1h lens at the maker toll and at no other. A limit resting AT the edge is the only entry that pays the maker
  fee, which is the only toll at which the 1h lens may trade a range. The 5m clock supplies timing and nothing
  else: an EMA cross toward value near the edge, or a failed 5m excursion beyond it. The trade is falsified by 1h
  acceptance beyond the faded edge and is bounded in time by the tuning-fit 1h traverse. The hazard is the fill
  itself — a resting limit is filled preferentially when price is going through it — so the row is judged on the
  book whose fills require a trade-through and is closed if it clears only when a touch is taken as a fill.
- **population:** the five home assets (L-D's home panel), pooled, both directions; lens of the clock 5m, lens of
  the value area 1h, permission from 1h and 4h; era HOLDOUT by the fill bar's close, `ERA_CUT < entry_close_ms`,
  with `ERA_CUT` = `research_outputs/tierc12/x_rec/tierc11x/pins/PINS_X.json["era_cut_ms"]`; scored window per
  O-9: `entry_close_ms ≤ W` and `exit_close_ms ≤ W` with `W` = TC11's pin
  (`research_outputs/tierc11/data/AS_OF_PIN.json["as_of_last_closed_4h_close_ms"]`), a position open at `W` marked
  there as `corridor_end`; the bars in (W, TC12's pin] are the forward strip — ridden for every arm, printed,
  never scored [L-S.25].
- **arms:**

    on row `k1` of `va_bars_1h` and row `k4` of `va_bars_4h`, the last lens bars with close ≤ τ, read as filed
    [L-S.3]. PERMISSION: 1h `state == INSIDE` and 4h state neither UNDEFINED nor accepted against the direction
    (ACCEPTED_BELOW for a long, ACCEPTED_ABOVE for a short), read once at τ [L-S.4]. SETUP: the 5m close's
    %-of-value against the in-force 1h profile between 0 and 33 inclusive for a long, between 67 and 100 inclusive
    for a short (33 / 67: contract :87; 0 and 100: the edges of value) [L-S.5]. TRIGGER: the engine EMA12 / EMA89
    (:89) of the 5m close crossing in the direction on that bar with the close within 0.25·ATR_1h (:90) of the
    edge on the value side, OR that close back inside value after the previous 5m close beyond the edge; a double
    trigger is a swing failure [L-S.6 … L-S.8]. ORDER: one unit at the edge snapped to the tick grid away from the
    market (a BUY limit floored, a SELL limit ceiled), all geometry frozen at τ; stop by `BK.brk_stop` from the
    limit — 0.5·ATR_1h (:97) beyond the swing failure's deviation extreme (every 5m low / high since the first
    close beyond, the return bar included), else from the limit, railed at 1.0·ATR_1h (:98; so R is exactly
    1.0·ATR_1h on cross orders); T1 = POC and T2 = far edge − 0.25·ATR_1h (:99) on the grid; REFUSED, with the
    first reason that holds, when the stop is undefined (`stop_none`), when T1 is not ahead of the limit
    (`poc_not_ahead`: `d·(n_T1 − n_L) ≤ 0`) or when T2 is not ahead of the limit (`t2_not_ahead`: `d·(n_T2 − n_L) ≤
    0`); T1 void when it lies at or beyond T2, the whole position then exiting at T2; a T1 within the round-trip
    taker fee of the limit is traded as written and flagged; SKIPPED (`rr_min`) iff `d·(T2 − L) / R < 1.5` (:100);
    valid for bars t+1 … t+12 (:92); cancelled at a 1h acceptance on the faded side; one resting order and one
    position per asset, a trigger meanwhile refused, never a replacement [L-S.9 … L-S.14]. FILL: the first valid
    bar with `low < limit − 1 tick` (long; :94) in exact integer ticks, at the limit price; no fill on a
    zero-volume bar [L-S.15]. WALK: on the fill bar the stop is tested and no target credited; then per 5m bar: a
    bar opening at or beyond the stop exits at the open; else the stop, adverse-first, at the stop price; then T1
    (half) at its level; then T2 (the rest) at its level, on the same bar if reached; a target fills by the same
    through-tick rule and books its level with no gap improvement; then at the close the invalidation at a 1h

### OPEN TO OPERATOR

1. **DEEP's floor.** The contract writes DEEP as "through by 0.05 ATR_1h" (:94-95). On part of the tape that is
   under one tick, where DEEP would be looser than the fill of record and "fails under DEEP too" would be read on
   a twin that is not deeper. DEFAULT if silent (O-32): DEEP = through by `max(0.05·ATR_1h, 1 tick)`, rounded up
   to whole ticks, with the share of orders where the floor binds printed per asset (L-S.15). The literal reading
   is the operator's to order; the per-order ladder assertion would then be dropped for the orders it breaks.
2. **A published maker rate at which X's edge leg is not above zero.** DEFAULT if silent: the row is built and
   scored, with the re-derived figure printed beside the word (O-19). Closing the row on it is the operator's
   order, by name, before Stage D's fee capture.
3. **The 17-asset view** needs the twelve's 5m tapes, which Stage D's sentence does not list (:19-20) and which the
   snapshot carries under O-8. DEFAULT if silent: built from those tapes, Tier-E, every row of the twelve labelled
   as carrying no licence (L-S.26). "NA for the twelve" is the alternative.
4. **One-asset dependence.** L-X.9 reads the LOAO clause as part of the kill (a TICK book that clears but fails
   LOAO 3/5 reads NOT SUPPORTED, qualifier `LOAO BELOW THE LINE (…)`); this section carries that rule. DEFAULT if
   silent (O-32): as L-X.9. Reading it as a qualifier on a SUPPORTED word is L-X.9's rival (ii), the operator's to
   name. The single-trade share has no threshold anywhere and decides nothing (L-X, OPEN TO OPERATOR 1).
5. **What CLOSED and CLOSED FOR GOOD forbid.** DEFAULT if silent: the standing lines of L-S.28, carried into the
   ledger append. The operator may word a closure's reach differently before the freeze; after a verdict it is an
   amendment that cannot follow from the outcome.
6. **CLOSED versus CLOSED FOR GOOD when TICK and DEEP fail and TOUCH clears.** Both contract clauses hold there
   (:104-105). DEFAULT if silent: `NOT SUPPORTED — CLOSED` (clears only under TOUCH), so that each clause has a
   live event; the literal-order rival (CLOSED FOR GOOD whenever TICK and DEEP fail) is the operator's to name.
   (The same item is L-X's OPEN TO OPERATOR 7.)
7. **The stop's else-clause never binds.** With the stop measured from the limit at the edge, "0.5 ATR_1h beyond
   the edge" (:97) is always inside the 1.0 ATR_1h rail (:98), so every cross-triggered order has R = 1.0·ATR_1h.
   DEFAULT if silent: the contract as written (the rail governs); the count of cross orders and `rail_binding` is
   printed. A cross stop at 0.5 ATR_1h with no rail is the operator's order.

**The fixture dialect** is L-0.14's. A leg is one `prove` call and one transcript block; a block id is `<FID>` or
`<FID> [<qualifier>]`, the qualifier a leg name, an instance (a directory or a grid) or `<leg> · <instance>`; a flow
leg of L-0.17 is the block `F-TYPED-FLOW [<pin name>]`. Inside a block the BREAK leg of named plants runs first and
each plant must be caught by its NAMED detector; then the REAL leg. A leg that cannot run prints NOT RUN, which is
never PASS; the tally line is `N GREEN, M RED, K NOT RUN`. No leg of this section makes a network call. Every suite
accepts `--root=DIR` and takes `--stage=<record id>` where it serves more than one record (never a leg filter). A
suite run at a record before `TC12-D` prints
`as_of_last_closed_4h: (pre-substrate stage)` and `substrate: none`. Fixture randomness is
`numpy.random.default_rng([E.SEED, crc32("<suite tag>|<block id>")])`, suite tags `forward`, `era`, `ferry`; the one
seeded draw of this section is F-ERA's pseudo-entries (count stated in L-L.23) — every other leg runs on the WHOLE of
a stated object and draws nothing.
**The port law** is L-D.11's, applied to three X sources: a ported function carries a provenance comment (source
file, lines, sha) and one label — VERBATIM (AST-identical to the X function), TEXT-ONLY (AST-identical once string
constants are blanked), CHANGED (the difference named in this section) or NEW. A literal inside a VERBATIM or
TEXT-ONLY port is the referee's (L-0.17 rule (G)); a module-level literal of an X source is READ from that source's
text by `ast.literal_eval`, never retyped; every CHANGED or NEW function holds structural literals only. Each suite
below carries a leg **F-PORT** that FAILS IF a port's label is untrue of the X text at its manifest sha (plants: one
token changed in a copy of a VERBATIM port; a comparator flipped in a copy of a TEXT-ONLY port; a provenance comment
naming another sha).

  (L-L.14), `scored` false. Its `prev_sha256` is `61ea177f…d89c`. Written at `TC12-REG.ledger-spec` by the spec
  tool. Lines 6 onward — rows, then one refresh line — are written at TC12-L (L-L.11, L-L.12).
- **Two guards `FL` does not have**, applied by TC12's `append` (a CHANGED port of `XF`:601-607) before each
  `FL.append_entry`: (i) the line must serialise under `allow_nan=False` (`FL` would write a bare `NaN`); (ii) no
  string value anywhere in the line may contain a character `c` for which `("a" + c + "b").splitlines()` has more
  than one element — `FL.read_lines` splits on `str.splitlines()`, and with `ensure_ascii=False` the characters
  U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029 are written raw and would split one line into two [measured here]. HALT `FWD-NAN` /
  `FWD-LINE-BREAK`.
- **Atomic write.** `FL.append_entry` appends in place and can leave a torn line. Every TC12 write therefore works
  on a scratch copy `T12/forward/_det_build/FORWARD_LEDGER.jsonl` (git-ignored): the record's bytes (X's bytes when
  the record is absent) are copied there; the lines are appended through the guards; the scratch is verified
  (`FL.verify_chain`, L-L.6, and `scratch_bytes.startswith(record_bytes)`); then `os.replace(scratch, record)`.
  This is TC11's writer law (`scripts/tierc11_forward_ledger.py`:406-411).
- **The commit law.** The ledger is append-only across commits (L-0.5 lists it APPEND-ONLY THROUGHOUT). It is
  recorded by two records — `TC12-REG.ledger-spec` (five lines), then `TC12-L` (rows and one refresh line) — which
  L-0.4's last-record law names as lawful: the working file verifies under `TC12-L`'s entry, and the earlier
  entry is held to the blob at the ledger-spec commit, whose bytes must also be a byte-prefix of the working file.
  A refresh that fails its suites before the TC12-L commit is quarantined (L-0.4) and the record restored to its
  last committed bytes, which the spec tool reproduces byte for byte. After the commit a wrong line is never
  edited: the remedy is an amendment and a re-opened ledger (L-L.3).

READING:

  (L-L.17): rows with `in_o9_scored_window == false` and, for `gated-v6-combined`, `entered_before_book_frozen ==
  false`. Both are counts of row lines; neither reads a row's outcome.

  filed value. On line 5 it is filed from the contract pin `ledger.n_min` (:110, `own n ≥ (\d+)`). HALT `FWD-NMIN`

  says how many of those rows a later score may read. Reaching `n_min` changes a status string and nothing else:

**L-L.17 THE LEDGER AND O-9's STRIP: THE OVERLAP WINDOW** — "re-ridden on the bars since 2026-09-21T16:00Z"
(contract :109); "the extension printed separately (the forward strip, never scored)" (:50); O-9
READING: the ledger opens at TC10's pin; O-9's strip opens at TC11's pin. The window between them,
`(OPENING_MS, E.TC11_PIN_MS]` — 2026-09-21T16:00Z to 2026-09-25T00:00Z, the 20 4h bars `T11/data/AS_OF_PIN.json`
counts under `bars_4h_past_tc10_pin` — lies INSIDE the scored window. A campaign whose entry bar closes in it is
both inside the window every registered row is scored on and admissible to the ledger. Stated plainly:
- **base v6, OLD-gated, combined-gated: NO such campaign exists.** TC11's filed v6 book holds 200 campaigns and
  none entered after TC10's pin; X's refresh line at the score edge reports, for `v6` and for `gated-v6-oldtide`,
  0 rows appended and no open key under the origin of record, and 0 closed admitted and no open key under the
  rival opening; the combined book is a subset of v6's rows. The base arm of P-ADM-1, P-BRD-1 and P-DIR-1 is that
  filed book, bit for bit (O-21). So no row of any registered arm is, or can become, a ledger row. The refresh
  asserts it — a v6 key with `OPENING_MS < entry_close_ms ≤ E.TC11_PIN_MS` HALTs `FWD-OVERLAP-V6` (it would
  contradict the filed book).
- **9/12: exactly ONE — the SOL campaign of L-L.13.** Its entry close (2026-09-24T20:00Z) is inside the scored
  window; it is admitted to the ledger. It belongs to NO registered arm of TC10, TC11, X or TC12: the 9/12 book's
  one registration was scored to TC10's pin, before this entry. What was seen of it is a mark at the score edge
  (filed in TC11's REFRESH line), not an exit. Under O-9 it is a row of the 9/12 book's scored-window table marked
  `corridor_end` at the score edge and is continued in the strip print; in the ledger it is a row when it closes.
- **The three flags — pin-independent, CHAINED on every row** (L-L.10; each a function of the row's
  `entry_close_ms` and of frozen instants):
  - `in_o9_scored_window` := `OPENING_MS < entry_close_ms ≤ W` (`W = E.TC11_PIN_MS`, the score edge);
  - `entered_before_gate_text_filed` := `entry_close_ms ≤` the STEP Q instant (L-D.1's object);
  - `entered_before_book_frozen` := `entry_close_ms ≤` the committer time (ms) of the commit that first adds line 5
    of `forward/FORWARD_LEDGER.jsonl`.
- **The freeze instant is filed ONCE,** in the write-once provenance record `T12/forward/BOOK4_FREEZE.json`
  `{commit, committer_time_ms, committer_time_iso, path, line}` — written by the orchestrator immediately after the
  `tierc12(TC12-REG.ledger-spec)` commit (the `STEP_Q.json` pattern: no builder runs git) and recorded by
  `TC12-D`'s record (L-0.5). The TC12-L builder reads it through `certified` and HALTs `FWD-FREEZE-ABSENT` if it
  is absent; F-FWD-OVERLAP holds it equal to git by a fixture-side read-only call (the F-D-PIN pattern).
- **What the refresh records:** `overlap` {`window` (the two instants), per book the admitted keys inside it};
  `freeze` (L-L.12); the three flags on every row line; `n_record` per book; the page's flag columns.
- **THE ROW SET OF RECORD FOR ANY LATER SCORE IS FIXED HERE,** in `BOOK_SPEC_COMBINED.json` → `n_law`, before a
  strip bar is on disk: rows with `in_o9_scored_window == false` and, for `gated-v6-combined`,
  `entered_before_book_frozen == false`. The all-rows figure is printed beside under the collar. No later
  registration chooses. The flagged rows count in `n` (the contract's count, :110) and not in `n_record`
  (L-L.14). The rule is fixed now because every appended row's `net_r` is printed on the page (L-L.15): a choice
  left to a later registration could not precede its look.
- **How TC11 and X handled the same overlap.** TC11 opened at TC10's pin "after which both frozen books are
  unseen" (L-T.6) while scoring to its own pin; its books carry the column `entered_after_tc10_pin`, and its ledger

  directory of L-L.32 and the quarantine directories `_det_partial_<…>/` of L-0.4; an extension outside

**L-L.26 NAMES, THE CSV DIALECT, THE READER LAW** — "→ exchange/rows/tierc12/ as CSV" (contract :111-112)
READING:
- **Bus path** `exchange/rows/tierc12/<name>.csv`; `<name>` = `flat_name(rel)` (VERBATIM, `XY`:481-485): the source
  path relative to `T12/`, extension dropped, each `/` written `__` (e.g. `forward__ledger_rows.csv`,
  `regbooks__P-ADM-1__scored.csv`). HALT `FERRY-NAME-COLLISION` on an exact or case-folded collision (`XY`:610-622).
  One `ROWS_MANIFEST.md` in the directory. The directory string is the contract pin `ferry.bus_dir` (:111, the
  one capture of `row file → (\S+)`, type str), read through the pin door and never typed.
- **Serializer** (`to_csv_bytes`, VERBATIM, `XY`:543-547): `df.to_csv(buf, index=False, lineterminator="\n",
  encoding="utf-8")`, the default float repr, the source's own row order, the source's own columns. The pandas
  version is recorded in the manifest.
- **Reader law** (X's AM-X15 (C), carried as text into the manifest and `ROWS_MANIFEST.md`): an untruncated CSV
  reads back equal to its parquet under `pandas.read_csv(<csv>, float_precision="round_trip",
  keep_default_na=False, na_values=[""], dtype=<the parquet schema's>)` — cell for cell, a null equal to a null,
  floats bit-equal; a string column's empty string reads back as a null. The default float parser is not lossless.

**L-L.28 THE BOX MEASURE AND THE THRESHOLDS** — "files that would push the box past WARN" (contract :112)
READING:
- **What is measured is the TICK SET, not `du`:** the tracked blobs under `SCOPE` (`exchange/`) plus `TICK_EXTRA`
  (`LEDGER.md`), at a PINNED commit of the main branch. Untracked files and the working copy of a modified file are
  not in it. The blobs are read in process from the git object store by ports of X's readers (`git_dir`,
  `read_ref`, `head_of`, the object reader and `tree_files`, VERBATIM, `XY`:764-1160); no TC12 module runs git.
  CHANGED: `box_at(head_sha)` sums the pinned commit's tree — TC12 builds in the target tree, so there is no merge
  target to compute. X's index cross-check is NOT carried: it HALTs whenever a tracked `exchange/` file is dirty,
  and the daily routine leaves one dirty every day.
- **The constants** — `SCOPE`, `BOX_BYTES`, `WARN_FRACTION`, `REFUSE_FRACTION`, `OVERRIDE_ENV`, `TICK_EXTRA`,
  `FLAG_BYTES` — are read by `ast.literal_eval` of their module-level assignments in `scripts/publish_exchange.py`
  (`publish_constants`, VERBATIM, `XY`:626-641); the module is never imported; its sha must be the census value
  (L-0.6).
- **The comparators** are `publish_exchange.budget`'s own (`level`, VERBATIM, `XY`:644-652): REFUSE iff the
  fraction is strictly above `REFUSE_FRACTION`; WARN iff it is at or above `WARN_FRACTION`; else OK. The WARN line
  in bytes is found on `level()` itself (`warn_line`, VERBATIM) and never typed.
- **"Past WARN"** is read as: the projection would leave OK — i.e. `publish()` would print its warning. A file is
  written iff `level(projection + its bytes) == "OK"`.
- `OVERRIDE_ENV` is never set; REFUSE is never overridden.

**L-L.29 THE FORECAST BASIS** — "files that would push the box past WARN are held" (contract :112); O-24 "staged
off-bus under `research_outputs/tierc12/ferry/` with a forecast"
SEAM SETTLEMENTS (`review/SEAM_PASS.json`, 2026-10-09 — part of this reading; each line governs where the text below is silent or differs):
- [seam 37] the reservation for TC12's own ledger append is sized from the STAGED file's byte count (L-X.32 makes the stamped and the staged counts equal by law).
READING: during the build the ferry writes nothing on the bus; it files a FORECAST. Two are filed: F1 at TC12-L and
F2 at TC12-CLOSE (when the draft and the staged append exist). Both use one law.
- **The pin.** `--pin` reads the main branch's HEAD sha from the ref files in process and writes it ONCE per stage
  to `T12/ferry/BOX_PIN_<STAGE>.json` — a provenance record — with the tick bytes at that commit and the measured
  parts below. Every forecast run and every fixture re-derives against the RECORDED sha, never the live HEAD; a
  moved HEAD is one printed line with no pass condition (AM-X17's law).
- **The projection base** = tick bytes at the pinned HEAD + the NAMED RESERVATIONS + the bytes of
  `ROWS_MANIFEST.md` (rendered in memory and reserved by X's monotone fixed point, `XY`:2233-2247). HALT if any

**L-L.30 THE HOLD LAW AND THE FROZEN ORDER** — "files that would push the box past WARN are held" (contract :112)

  order is WRITTEN iff `level(cumulative + its carried bytes) == "OK"`, else it is **HELD FOR ATHENA** — not
  written, not counted — and the loop CONTINUES (a later, smaller file may still be written). If the base alone
  reads WARN, every file is held. HALT `FERRY-REFUSE`, writing nothing, only if the base alone is past REFUSE.
- **The order, frozen here before any size exists** (file sizes are structural, but an order chosen after they
  are known is a selection):
  1. `forward/ledger_rows.parquet` — the ledger's appended rows (the contract's §0 item, :127);
  2. the `scored` arm of each registration, in the registry's `seq` order (read from the registry, not typed);
  3. every `base` arm that a `STATUS.json` lists (the two-sample registrations), in `seq` order, then
     P-SCALP-3's `ladder__touch` and `ladder__deep` (the fill-sensitivity row is part of that verdict's text);
  4. every other FERRIED file — the `strip` and `tierE__*` arms among them — by source path, ascending bytewise.
  A file of positions 1-3 that does not exist (a row closed by precondition lists no arm; a ledger with no
  appended row writes no `ledger_rows`) is skipped and printed `ABSENT (<reason>)`.
- Every WRITTEN bus file over `FLAG_BYTES` is FLAGGED: named to the operator, with its home, in the forecast, in
  `ROWS_MANIFEST.md` and in the report's file-disposition table.

**L-L.32 STAGING OFF-BUS, AND THE FERRY OF RECORD AS A CLOSE ACT** — O-24 "the ferry of record into

READING: `scripts/tierc12_ferry.py` (shim-armed; a decision module; it holds no subprocess site and runs no git)
has three modes. In none of them does a python source write under `exchange/`: the shim refuses it (L-D.27) and
L-0.8's F-OFFBUS scans for it. The ferry is a carrier: it reads each table whole through pandas, derives a class

It selects no value-area column by name, hands no lens to the reader, and its declared VA read list is empty.
- `--stage=<TC12-L | TC12-CLOSE>`: enumerate `T12/` (never typed), triage, class each tabular file (typed list and
  rule), serialise and cut each FERRIED file, and write the carried CSV to `T12/ferry/_det_staged/<name>.csv` — a
  directory the nested ignore rule already keeps out of git and the triage excludes from enumeration. Each source
  is hashed, read once, hashed again. `FERRY_MANIFEST.json` records per file: tier, rel, source sha and bytes,
  rows, columns, declared key, typed class, the rule's class, kind, reason, and the CSV facts (the carried sha
  among them). The run at TC12-CLOSE re-enumerates (files written after TC12-L exist then) and re-stages any
  source whose sha moved.

  then `TC12-CLOSE` (re-filed with `forecast_TC12-CLOSE`) — which L-0.4's last-record law names as lawful: the
  working file verifies under the later entry and the earlier entry is held to the blob at the TC12-L commit. The
  staged CSVs are NOT entries of a record's `artifact_shas`: they are scratch derivations under a `_det_`
  directory, pinned by their carried sha in that tracked manifest and re-derivable byte for byte from their
  sources. (A review worktree stages parquet and never a `_det_*` path, L-0.12; a recorded path it cannot stage
  would read RECORDED NOT STAGED.) `F-ROWS [EXIST]` re-derives each of them and `F-ROWS [FRESH]` re-hashes them
  where they stand.
- `--pin` then `--forecast` (L-L.29, L-L.30): the pin record, the manifest's forecast block, the forecast page.
- `--of-record` — run ONLY by the operator's `close_acts.sh`, at its step 2, after its step 0 has proven the
  TC10, TC11 and X blocks landed by bytes in that order (L-X.33): it pins the HEAD of that instant; measures the
  tick set with the three closes inside it; reserves ONLY TC12's own close adds (the draft, the staged append, the
  two stamp lines, `ROWS_MANIFEST.md`) and that instant's `swept`; re-hashes every source and every staged CSV
  against the tracked manifest (a moved or missing file STOPS the act); runs the first-fit; and writes, under
  `T12/ferry/` only, `OF_RECORD.json` (the pin, the measure, the projection, the WRITTEN / HELD / FLAGGED sets) and
  `of_record/ROWS_MANIFEST.md` and `of_record/COPY_LIST.txt`.
- **The copy is the shell's.** `close_acts.sh` creates `exchange/rows/tierc12/`, copies each listed staged CSV and
  the rendered `ROWS_MANIFEST.md` there, and compares shas; then runs the suite in its act mode,
  `scripts/tierc12_ferry_fixtures.py --of-record` (L-L.33), whose transcript `ferry/of_record/F_ROWS_AT_CLOSE.txt`

  script STOPS. `publish()` at its own step stages the bus files; the script stages no `exchange/` path itself.
- The executor never runs `--of-record` in the main tree and never creates `exchange/rows/` (O-12). Its only
  executions of `--of-record` are inside fixtures, against scratch repositories (`F-ROWS [ACT]`); in the acts'

`TC12-L` is not in L-0.10's parallel set: it starts only when every earlier entry of `RESUME_ORDER_T` is
COMPLETE-VERIFIED. Its record's `depends_on` names every blocking record from `TC12-REG` on that precedes it — the
ferry stages every stage's row files; the ledger reads the records `TC12-REG.ledger-spec`, `TC12-D`, `TC12-ENV`,
`TC12-ENV.score-build`, `TC12-C`, `TC12-V.stamps.c` and `TC12-G`; the era reads `TC12-C` and `TC12-G` — so a
quarantine of any of them makes `TC12-L` PARTIAL with it. The stage has three producers: each returns its artifact
map and the record `progress/TC12-L.json` is written from the three by the orchestrator's gate step (L-0.10's rule
for a record with several producers), with one fixture entry per suite (`forward`, `era`, `ferry`).

Compute: no worker pool in any of the three; the ledger rides twice per book family (the pin and the look-back
anchor) plus two re-ride rivals, in one process. Fixture subprocesses — the era's mirror process, the F-DET twins —
run one at a time (O-5).

L-L owns no registered row and files no registration: Stage L files a diary, Tier-E tables and row files; none
carries a hypothesis, a family, a bar or a verdict word, and no spec block of this section is carried into the
registry. One clause of an owner's spec is worded here, and L-G's P-ADM-1 block carries it verbatim:
- **P-ADM-1 (L-G), `disclosed_beside`:** "the forward ledger's fourth book `gated-v6-combined` — its spec
  `research_outputs/tierc12/forward/BOOK_SPEC_COMBINED.json` (sha filed at TC12-REG.ledger-spec); every row
  appended at TC12's pin entered before the book was frozen (flagged on the row) and none is a row of record for
  confirmation; `n` appended at TC12's pin, UNSCORED until its own n ≥ n_min; Tier-E, no verdict word; it is the
  contract's 'confirmation' (:55-56) and none of it is scored here."

  precondition of a registration in it; the tie between the two runs the other way — the spec carries
  `p_adm_1_payload_sha256` and the sha of the one `scored` element (L-L.2), and F-FWD-SPEC holds both to the filed
  registry.

### OPEN TO OPERATOR

1. **Which ledger is of record for base v6 and 9/12 from now on.** Default if silent: TC12's file, from its first
   refresh line (O-24); TC11's file stays at 0 rows and is never refreshed; X's two lines keep their frozen role
   text "X twin — TC11's ledger not yet opened", printed beside TC12's statement.
2. **The one campaign that is both inside the scored window and on the ledger** (9/12, SOL, entered
   2026-09-24T16:00Z). Default if silent: when it closes it is appended, counts in the 9/12 book's `n`, carries
   the chained flag `in_o9_scored_window`, and is NOT a row of record for any later score — the rows of record are
   fixed in `n_law` (L-L.17); the all-rows figure is printed beside. Keeping it off the ledger altogether, or
   counting it as a row of record, is the operator's order.
3. **"The gated books" of the era clause.** Default if silent: the ledger's two gated books (OLD-gated,
   combined-gated) beside v6. Tabling the kept books of P-BRD-1 or P-DIR-1 as well is an order, not a reading.
4. **The box.** On the filed figures the three pending closes alone bring the box to the WARN line. Default if
   silent: every TC12 row file that would leave OK is HELD FOR ATHENA and listed; `ROWS_MANIFEST.md` and the report
   land under `publish()`'s warning; REFUSE is never overridden. Releasing held files, the cap (the contract's
   2 MB against the bus's 1,048,576 B per file) and a rotation rule for `exchange/rows/` are ATHENA's (Q-A1, Q-A2).
5. **The closing order.** Default if silent: TC12's ferry of record refuses until X's block has landed. Closing
   TC12 before X would change which of X's files are held; only the operator can order it.
6. **The next refresh.** Each refresh is a data spend at a new pin. Default if silent: none after the one line at
   TC12's pin; the ledger waits for a later tier or an operator order.
7. **The fourth book's backdated origin.** The contract opens all four books at 2026-09-21T16:00Z; the fourth
   book's gate text was filed at STEP Q and its spec was frozen on the chain at the ledger-spec commit, both after
   TC12's pin, so every row of this refresh predates both (L-L.17). Default if silent (O-32): the contract's
   origin stands; every such row is appended, counted in `n`, and carries the chained flags
   `entered_before_gate_text_filed` and `entered_before_book_frozen`; the rows of record are fixed in `n_law`
   (L-L.17) — for the fourth book, rows entered after the freeze instant — so its `n_record` is 0 at this
   refresh; the all-rows figure is printed beside. Moving the origin itself, or taking STEP Q in place of the
   freeze instant as the binding flag, is the operator's order.
8. **The row set of record for a later forward score is fixed now.** It is the contract's "confirmation" of
   P-ADM-1 (:55-56) that is at stake. Default if silent: `n_law` as L-L.17 words it — a row inside O-9's scored
   window is never of record for any book, a fourth-book row entered before the book was frozen is never of record
   — and no later registration may choose otherwise. Changing the rule after this text is frozen needs an
   amendment and a re-opened ledger (L-L.3).
9. **The 1w block is left out of the ledger's side table.** Default if silent: `ledger_side` copies the 1h, 4h,
   12h and 1d blocks of the entry stamp and points to the stamp row for the rest (O-28: the 1w block has exactly
   two readers). Carrying it into a table that reaches the bus is an order that would amend O-28.
